discovery: Discovery of the hidden simplicity of gauge-theory scattering amplitudes and the on-shell methods built on it, which made precision QCD predictions for the LHC possible

nominees.name: Zvi Bern
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

subfield: Theoretical particle physics (quantum field theory, scattering amplitudes, collider phenomenology)
motivation: In 1986 Parke and Taylor found that multi-gluon amplitudes, which Feynman diagrams express as thousands of terms, collapse to a single line: the maximally-helicity-violating formula. This showed that gauge theory has a structure that Lagrangians hide. Bern, with collaborators, turned that insight into the unitarity method, which builds loop amplitudes from on-shell tree amplitudes alone. These methods made possible the next-to-leading-order QCD predictions for multi-jet, W/Z+jets and top-quark backgrounds that the LHC needed for Higgs measurements and new-physics searches. They now underpin precision collider theory and the modern on-shell construction of effective field theories such as SMEFT, and they have been applied to gravitational-wave templates. This is a rare case where a formal discovery about quantum field theory changed what experiments can measure and how we interpret the data.
